html:
The Kotiria, also called Wanano, are an Eastern Tukanoan people of the middle Vaupés River on the border of Colombia and Brazil. Like their neighbours, they practise linguistic exogamy, marrying outside their own language group, so most Kotiria homes hold speakers of two or more languages, often Tukano and Tuyuka or Desana.

They fish, grow bitter manioc and live in riverside villages ranked by the order of their ancestors in myth. Rubber traders and Catholic missions reached them in the late 1800s and 1900s. Fewer than two thousand people speak the language today.
